thesis: Compile desired end states into explicit causal intervention architectures, beginning with bounded known causal models and expanding only as evidence supports broader substrates.

claims.statement: Given a correct finite causal model, a desired target state and declared controllable variables, an algorithm can compile interventions whose cardinality is globally minimum within that declared model.
claims.falsifier: A preregistered case exists where the compiler returns the wrong satisfiability status or an intervention set larger than the exhaustive global minimum.
assumptions: The supplied causal model and equations are correct for the tested system.
Declared controllable variables are the only allowed interventions.
requiredEvidence: Independent correctness comparison against exhaustive or formally verified minima.
Adversarial graph structures including shared upstream causes.

claims.statement: Causal structure and desired-state semantics can reduce intervention-search work relative to uninformed enumeration without changing the exact minimum.
claims.falsifier: Under preregistered matched benchmarks, the compiler fails to reduce computational work or changes the correct minimum intervention.
assumptions: The causal graph exposes exploitable structure.
requiredEvidence: Held-out efficiency comparison with full accounting.

claims.statement: A sufficiently general causal compiler could transfer the desired-state-to-intervention pattern across computational, physical, biological and economic systems.
claims.falsifier: After representation, measurement and authority constraints are satisfied, the common causal interface repeatedly fails to preserve intervention semantics across independently tested substrate classes.
assumptions: Cross-domain causal descriptions can share a useful intermediate representation.
Relevant causal structure can be identified at actionable fidelity.
requiredEvidence: At least two non-synthetic substrate demonstrations.

constraints.description: The compiler cannot be more correct than the causal structure and equations supplied or discovered.
Exact intervention optimization may become combinatorial for general causal graphs and action spaces.
Physical, biological and economic use requires measurable state variables and outcome observability.
Real interventions on external systems require explicit authority independent of capability.
Interventions can create side effects outside the modeled target and require containment and reconciliation.
Real-world interventions must remain within applicable law, consent and rights constraints.

unknowns: causal structure discovery from incomplete observations
currentParentStateReason: The moonshot has a formal claim decomposition and explicit constraint map. Only a narrow computational child mechanism has software evidence; the cross-substrate thesis remains uncertain.
nextGates: independent or native replication of V2
authorized non-synthetic proxy only after prior gates
